title: Happy-Path Monoculture
pattern: A test suite consisting entirely of success scenarios ("happy path") while completely omitting tests for errors, edge cases, boundaries, or failure recovery paths.
why_bad: In real production environments, systems run in a hazardous world (out-of-bounds inputs, disk failures, network drops) [569]. Leaving failure paths untested is a major source of reliability defects and security vulnerabilities [27, 270].
detection: The complete absence of tests asserting error types, limits, exceptions, timeouts, or negative bounds.
counterexample: Tests verifying correct recovery and bounds (e.g., passing invalid parameters, empty files, or simulated network errors) [498].
fix: Systematically test limits (maximums, minimums, off-by-one bounds), empty conditions, and use fault-injection simulators to verify error recovery [267, 270, 498].
source:
*   *The Pragmatic Programmer*, "Ruthless Testing: Boundary Conditions" (Topic 41) [267, 569, 573]
*   *Release It!*, "Emulate out-of-spec failures / Happy Path" (p. 239) [270, 597]
*   *Building Secure and Reliable Systems*, "Testing Error Handling Paths" (p. 239) [27, 391]
